evidence_adequacy.verdict: THIN: 5 transitions constrain rank 3 of 679 features, so the null space has dimension 676 and nearly every vector in it is a 'law' that is true over these states and unfalsified rather than confirmed. Treat every law below as a correlation awaiting a transition that could break it, not as a conservation law.

log.subject: colour-0 dynamic cells
log.why: twelve cells form the interior ring of the 6x6 case at rows 37-40 x cols 12-15 in the current frame, and they lie inside the t1/t2 change box, so they are dynamic and need an owner.

log.subject: colour-1 dynamic cells
log.why: eight of them are named cell-by-cell in the t3/t4/t5 diffs as slot cells, and the ninth is the case socket at (38,16); all nine are inside the t1/t2 box.

log.subject: colour-2 dynamic cells
log.why: four slot cells named in the diffs, four rail-marker cells at rows 32-33 x cols 13-14, the socket at (39,16), and the bar end (53,63) whose 2->3 burn is the only diff outside the arena box.

log.subject: colour-3 dynamic cells
log.why: eight cells of the rail track at rows 30-31 and 34-35 x cols 13-14; row 29 of the same track is outside the dynamic rows and is board.

log.subject: colour-4 dynamic cells
log.why: twelve of them by subtraction only -- 97 dynamic minus the 85 I can name from the frame -- so this is the weakest declaration here and it is flagged as derived in the invariant.

log.subject: colour-5 dynamic cells
log.why: 24 background-coloured cells at cols 11-12 and 15-16 x rows 30-35; the t1 diff lists 5 among the changed colours, and 97 minus cells_needing_an_owner 73 is exactly 24, which is the independent check.

log.subject: colour-6 dynamic cells
log.why: 22 cells of the case border and its 2x2 core, all inside the t1/t2 change box.

log.subject: mdl_segmenter obj0/obj2/obj3 (13x36, ~440 cells)
log.why: a 440-cell track cannot be one instance and a second type over pixels my seven colours already own would double-claim them; I take only its cell counts, 440/436/440, as the sole quantitative fact I have about the hidden state s1.

log.subject: mdl_segmenter obj1 (2x54, 108 cells, all frames)
log.why: rejected as an object for the same extent reason, accepted as evidence: it fixes the bar at rows 53-54 x cols 10-63, so the bar is 54 cells wide and does not start at col 0.

log.subject: the inherited Glyph9/Vacated/Spent/Dark declarations
log.why: no dynamic cell here has frame-0 colour 9, so Glyph9 would seat nothing, while Spent and Dark would seat on my colour-1 and colour-0 cells and fire panel rules that no transition in this evidence stream witnesses.

log.subject: key3_clears_strip_tok1
log.why: t3 lists eight colour-1 slot cells going 1->4 and no others; the guard colored(above(above(?p)), 4) is true of exactly those eight among all Tok1 instances and false of the socket at (38,16), whose two-above is colour 6.

log.subject: key3_clears_strip_tok2
log.why: the same transition lists four colour-2 slot cells going 2->4; the same guard excludes the rail marker (two-above is 3) and the bar end (two-above is 5).

log.subject: key7_clears_strip_tok1 / key7_clears_strip_tok2
log.why: t5 reproduces t3 cell for cell under a different key; the bodies are identical and I cannot merge them because the guard grammar has no disjunction and no action domain.

log.subject: key4_redraws_strip_tok1 / key4_redraws_strip_tok2
log.why: t4 restores each of the twelve slot cells to its frame-0 colour, and typing by frame-0 colour is what lets two rules with integer-literal targets reproduce a 2-1-1/1-1-2 pattern without naming a single coordinate.

log.subject: key4_burns_bar_end
log.why: (53,63) 2->3 at t4 is the only diff outside the arena; rightof(?p) = wall picks it out of the ten Tok2 instances uniquely, and its colour guard is disjoint from the redraw rule's so the pair cannot both fire.

log.subject: any rule for ACTION1 or ACTION2
log.why: 96 cells changed on each and I was given only the count and bounding box, never a pixel; writing a guessed rule would trade a known-wrong silence for an invented change, and constraint 2 forbids the entry.

log.subject: burn_next (the leading-edge bar rule)
log.why: text written out inside i_cannot_draw_a_burn_on_a_cell_that_has_never_changed; it stays out until a second burn makes (53,62) dynamic, because a cell the board still explains gets no instance and the rule would be cov 0/0.

log.subject: s2 = s0, so ACTION2 undoes ACTION1
log.why: distinct_states is 5 for 6 states, so exactly one pair coincides, and t2 restored exactly the 96 cells t1 changed while t3/t4/t5 each changed a strict subset -- no other pairing is consistent.

log.subject: burns iff the command index is even
log.why: command index 2 was even and did not burn; the reading that dominated the inherited manual is refuted on the first transition that could test it here.

log.subject: the bar burn is keyed to ACTION4 rather than to the redraw effect
log.why: one positive and four negatives fit both readings identically because t4 is the only transition that redrew the slot; one press of ACTION4 on an already-drawn slot separates them.

log.subject: cells_needing_an_owner 73 = 97 minus the 24 background-coloured dynamic cells
log.why: the 24 was derived from the frame before the store number was consulted, so the agreement is a check and not a fit; it is the reason I trust the whole census.

log.subject: zero_space global law over 97 cells
log.why: its cell list is my census restated; it self-reports THIN at rank 3 of 679 features over 5 transitions, so it confirms nothing beyond which cells move.

log.subject: cegis_miner verdict, the world does not narrate as one mover
log.why: correct here and not merely an arm limitation -- every observed event is a recolour in place and nothing in six frames translates.

log.subject: make the ACTION1 successor the state the round ends in
log.why: diffs are printed cell by cell only for small changes, so the 96-cell state s1 can only be read off the current-frame print; it is the largest single purchase available.

log.subject: press ACTION4 with the slot already drawn
log.why: separates the key-keyed bar reading from the effect-keyed one; the answer must be read off the raw diff because the next bar cell is board and undrawable either way.

log.subject: press ACTION3 or ACTION7 with the slot already blank
log.why: witnesses a silence my manual asserts on no evidence, and any change at all refutes the clear rules as written.

log.subject: press ACTION5 or ACTION6
log.why: two of seven keys have never been pressed in this world and my manual asserts total inertness for both on the strength of nothing.

log.subject: no way to say unobserved, the manual declines to predict
log.why: I wanted a third outcome for (state, action) beyond a named successor and identity; what I wrote instead is no rule at all for keys 1 and 2 plus a theorem posting the exact 96-pixel bill, because the compiled step is total and turns my ignorance into a confident silence.

log.subject: no disjunction and no action domain in the guard grammar
log.why: I wanted one clear rule guarded on key(3) or key(7); what I wrote instead is four rules with two identical bodies, declared in a theorem as a cost paid to the DSL rather than a claim about the world.

log.subject: no arithmetic across types in an invariant body
log.why: I wanted one invariant asserting the seven instance counts sum to 97; what I wrote instead is eight separate count invariants plus the summation spelled out in the census theorem.
